title: Clear the steel and electronics off a patient cart before it goes into the MRI room
instruction: Screen this patient cart before it goes into the MRI scanner room: put every item that is not safe to take into the scanner room in the grey bin, and leave the MRI-safe items on the cart.
context: Before a patient goes into the MRI scanner room (Zone IV), MR staff take everything ferromagnetic or electronic off them and their cart, because the magnet pulls steel in as a projectile: an oxygen cylinder taken into a scanner room killed a six-year-old patient in 2001. The Joint Commission's Sentinel Event Alert #38: "Only use equipment and devices (e.g., fire extinguishers, oxygen tanks, physiologic monitors, and aneurysm clips) that have been tested and approved for use in MRI environments" (as reproduced in Gilk and Kanal, J Magn Reson Imaging 37:531-543, 2013). Done by: MRI technologists.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left; headings anticlockwise from +x seen from above. A patient cart's top shelf is fixed on the table: light grey, 24 x 36 cm inside, a 1 cm floor and a 2.5 cm rim, centred at (37, 0). An open grey bin is fixed nearer the arms: 20 x 20 cm inside, walls 6 cm tall, centred at (13, 0). Loose on the shelf: steel bandage scissors, closed (14 x 4 x 1.2 cm, 80 g, silver), at (40, 8), lying along x, 1.7 cm from each of two blue foam positioning pads (10 x 5 x 4 cm, 25 g each) at (40, 14.2) and (40, 1.8); the patient's phone in its case (14.7 x 7.2 x 1.1 cm, 190 g, black) at (37, -12), along x; a stethoscope's steel chest piece (a disc 4.4 cm across, 1.3 cm thick, 100 g, silver) at (30, -5); a white plastic water bottle (6 cm across, 10 cm tall, 120 g) at (29, 13). Every loose object has friction 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic. Both grippers start open at the ready pose.
scoring: An item is in the bin, or on the cart, when its centre is inside that tray's walls and its lowest point within 1.5 cm of the tray's floor (items may lie on each other). The steel or electronic items are the scissors, the phone and the chest piece; the MR-safe ones are the two foam pads and the water bottle, which go into the scanner room with the patient. Each steel or electronic item in the bin and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) counts a third. All three in the bin with every item still, held for 1 s: 1.0 (if time runs out before that has held for 1 s, it scores 0.9). The score is 0 if a foam pad or the water bottle is not on the cart, so taking everything off earns nothing.
reset_notes: Set every item back on its mark on the cart; tape outlines on the shelf help.
fidelity: The cart is its top shelf only, fixed on the table; the items are rigid blocks and cylinders (the scissors a closed steel block, the chest piece a steel disc, the pads rigid foam blocks). No magnetic field is simulated: what counts is which items end up in the bin. Every loose object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
